sourceBindings.text: Use the measured plot evidence from the previous step to write a one-page plan. A useful plan links each concern to a test, an intervention, a reason and a check of whether the intervention worked. It keeps the original class activity and crop lists while refusing to invent a site-specific dose.

Diagnose three evidence-based concerns in the 10 m × 10 m plot and sequence tests, drainage/water decisions and amendments in a one-page plan rather than treating compost as a substitute for salt management.
Compare compost, aged manure, biochar, mulch, windbreaks, cover crops and water-management options, explaining benefits, costs and site limits without prescribing an unverified rate.
Choose two candidate crops, justify drought and salt tolerance separately, and check method-matched ECe, cultivar, establishment stage, irrigation water and economics before a real planting decision.

sourceBindings.text: In 5 minutes list three site concerns, their measured evidence or missing method, and one crop impact each. Keep 10 m × 10 m, 0.8%, 3.5 dS/m and borewell description intact.

In 10 minutes sequence tests, water/drainage decision, amendment-quality check, surface management and follow-up measurement. Compare at least three distinct techniques and explain why the teacher's layer depths are proposals rather than a site dose.
In 5 minutes choose two of the source crops and write one sentence for drought fit and one for salt fit for each, plus one missing site, cultivar or growth-stage datum.

During the final five-minute discussion phase in total, two or three groups share the one-page plan. Answer a peer challenge about water, amendment amount or crop choice. Complete the original exit ticket on organic matter and two benefits, then state what that answer does not prove.
Separate measured values from interpretations; do not call 3.5 moderately saline before method is known.

Online planning practice. Soil extraction, water chemistry, drainage, material analysis and crop conditions remain incomplete. Saved words or a complete form do not approve an application rate, crop yield or practical pass.

sourceBindings.text: rehabilitation plan
A site-specific sequence connecting evidence, action, reason and follow-up observation.
organic amendment
An added material such as suitable compost, aged manure or biochar; composition, salts and rate need separate assessment.
biochar
Carbon-rich material made by heating biomass with limited oxygen; effects depend on feedstock, processing, soil and rate.
mulch
Surface cover such as straw, wood chips or gravel used to influence evaporation, temperature, weeds or erosion.
windbreak
A vegetation barrier planned to reduce wind speed and erosion, with possible water, light and land competition.
cover crop
A crop grown primarily for ground cover and soil effects rather than the main harvest; it still needs water and local suitability.
leaching
Dissolved salt movement below the root zone with suitable water and a functioning drainage outlet.
ECe
Electrical conductivity of a saturated soil-paste extract; compare only with a table using the same method and units.
ECw
Electrical conductivity of irrigation water, different from soil ECe.
halophyte
A plant naturally adapted to strongly saline environments; a conventional crop with some salt tolerance is not automatically one.
cultivar
A selected crop variety whose response may differ from other varieties of the same species.
rootstock
The rooted plant onto which a fruit-tree scion is grafted; it can change pistachio responses to salinity and other conditions.
